title: KV micro-partitioning and latency-aware prefetch coordinator for multi-GPU KV cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a coordinated multi-GPU strategy to shard KV cache at a finer granularity (micro-partitions / hot-chunks) and proactively prefetch these shards in a latency-aware manner during continuous batching. The goal is to improve p50/p95/p99 latency and reduce cross-GPU stalls while keeping GPU memory utilization predictable for large mixed workloads (chat + stream + short completion).

Background: 
Existing slab and stripe sharding strategies work well for steady-state hot sets, but they suffer from two problems under continuous batching and mixed tensor/pipeline parallel topologies: (1) bursty temporal hot keys create short-lived imbalances causing cross-GPU fetchs that block generation; (2) coarse shard granularity forces either over-replication or large remote transfers that inflate tail latency and memory pressure.

Goal and success criteria:
- Implement a KV micro-partitioning + latency-aware prefetch coordinator that: (a) partitions KV entries into 64KB-512KB micro-partitions (configurable), (b) tracks temporal affinity windows per request stream, and (c) schedules prefetches aligned with continuous-batching windows to hide transfer latency.
- Acceptance criteria: under the synthetic mixed-chat workload (token rate 45k/s, 32 concurrent sessions): reduce cross-GPU blocking events by >=60%, improve p99 generation token latency by >=20% vs current slab baseline, and keep additional GPU memory overhead <= 8% on average.

Design overview: 
1) Micro-partition unit: default 128KB (tunable). Partitions are contiguous KV-entry ranges forming "hot-chunks". The runtime exposes mapping metadata so the placement layer can reason about chunk boundaries during tensor/pipeline parallel mapping.

2) Placement heuristic: hybrid affinity-driven placement. We maintain a per-session frequency sketch and a short-term temporal affinity window (default 3s). Chunks exceeding an affinity threshold are promoted to local-GPU residency; cold chunks are left remote and prefetched on demand.

3) Prefetch coordinator: a centralized (per-node) coordinator schedules prefetches on batch boundaries emitted by the continuous batching engine. Prefetch scheduling considers: (a) current batch composition and aggregated future token horizon, (b) RDMA/peer-bandwidth budget, (c) overlapping pipeline stage execution windows, and (d) memory headroom. Prefetches are throttled to preserve latency SLOs and avoid head-of-line blocking.

4) Interaction with tensor/pipeline parallelism: 
- Tensor parallel shards keep model weight shards local as before. KV micro-partitions are associated with (tensor-shard-id, pipeline-stage-id) pairs so that placement respects compute locality.
- During pipelined execution, the coordinator signals prefetch timing aligned to the downstream stage's expected KV access window to ensure KV is resident before the stage begins. This reduces cross-stage stalls and duplicate transfers.

5) Eviction & spill policy: 
- Eviction uses an affinity-aware LRU that biases against evicting currently promoting hot-chunks.
- Spill hierarchy: GPU -> local host DRAM -> remote peer -> disk (last resort). Spill is done asynchronously with prioritized rehydration when the affinity window indicates imminent reuse.

6) Consistency and correctness: 
- KV cache entries are immutable during generation (read-only semantics). Prefetch/evict operations are race-free since requests will either wait for the prefetch completion or fallback to on-demand fetch with a short backoff.
- For sessions pinned to dedicated capacity, we allow an opt-in strong-residency mode (no remote fetches) to preserve strict latency guarantees.

Runtime configuration knobs (initial): 
- kv.micro_partition_size = 131072
- kv.prefetch_window_ms = 2000
- kv.max_gpu_kv_bytes = 0.85 * gpu_kv_capacity
- kv.spill_strategy = "host_async_priority"
- kv.affinity_threshold = 0.12
- kv.rebalance_period_s = 60

Telemetry and observability additions: 
- kv.micropartitions.count, kv.prefetch.requests, kv.prefetch.success_rate, kv.prefetch_latency_p95, kv.evictions.count, kv.spill.bytes_host, kv.remote_fetch.bytes, kv.prefetch_hit_rate_by_route, kv.batch_alignment_skew_ms.
- Add per-route dashboard panels and SLO alerts if prefetch_hit_rate < 70% or prefetched_bytes > budget for >2 min.

Testing and rollout plan: 
- Unit tests for partition mapping and coordinator scheduling.
- Integration tests: multi-GPU CI harness with heterogeneous sequence length distributions.
- Canary rollout: runtime flag opt-in, initial target: 5% hosted traffic on a low-risk model family. Monitor latency/p95/p99 and memory pressure.

Migration path: 
- Start in "stateless opt-in" mode: coordinator only suggests placement; no automatic eviction.
- Progress to "managed placement" for dedicated pools after load testing.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Micro-partitioning reduces transfer size but increases mapping metadata; we mitigate using compact partition indices and bloom sketches.
- Centralized coordinator simplifies scheduling but introduces a single node actor; we shard coordinators per-physical-host and design failover to local on-demand fetches.

Risks: 
- Prefetch mispredictions could worsen tail latency under adversarial mixes — mitigation: conservative thresholds and immediate fallback to on-demand remote fetch.
- Increased CPU overhead for frequency tracking — mitigation: approximate sketches and sampling.

Acceptance tests & benchmarks to add to repo: 
- bench/kv_micropart_bench.py (synthetic hot/cold mixes)
- perf dashboards: infra/kv-micropart/2026-03-loadtest (link below)

Links & artifacts: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/KV+Micropartitioning+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4982
- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/kv-micropart/kv-micropart-loads

Notes: 
- This ticket focuses on the placement and prefetch coordinator. The micro-partition compaction/merge heuristics will be a follow-on (ENG-62746).
updates: 2026-02-26 - Initial spike: prototype coordinator that listens to batch events and issues prefetches on a local dev rig. Observed 35% reduction in blocking events for short sequences.

2026-03-02 - Design review w/ infra and runtime: agreed on 128KB default partition size; decided to shard coordinator per-physical-host rather than fully centralized. Action: update failure modes and failover behavior.
2026-03-05 - PM feedback (Priya Desai): add route-level opt-in and telemetry for per-customer debugging. Added kv.prefetch_* metrics to telemetry list.

2026-03-08 - Security review note (Jonas Berg): RDMA transfers must respect KMS/E2E constraints for Private deployments. We will disable RDMA prefetch in Private by default and fall back to encrypted host-transfer path.

2026-03-12 - Engineering sync: created prototype PR (runtime/pull/4982). Performance run on 8xA10 nodes shows p99 token latency down 18% and remote transfer bytes down 42% in mixed workload. Need longer run for steady-state memory overhead measurement.
